title: What Is Version Control?
summary: What version control is, the local/centralized/distributed models, why Git is distributed and stores snapshots not diffs, and the essential Git-vs-GitHub distinction.

title: Installing & Configuring Git
summary: Install Git on any OS, set your commit identity, and understand Git's three config levels (system, global, local) — plus the settings worth changing on day one.

title: The Three States & Your First Commit
summary: The working tree, the staging area (index), and the repository — and the add → commit workflow that moves changes between them to create your first snapshot.

title: Viewing & Ignoring History
summary: Read history with git log, inspect changes with git diff (working vs staged vs committed), and keep junk out of your repo with .gitignore — including why it only affects untracked files.

title: Undoing Things
summary: Fix mistakes safely: amend the last commit, unstage and discard changes with git restore, understand the three git reset modes, and undo shared commits with git revert.

title: Branching Basics
summary: A branch is just a movable pointer to a commit, and HEAD marks where you are. Create, switch, and delete branches — and understand what a detached HEAD means.

title: Merging & Conflicts
summary: Combine branches with git merge: when Git can fast-forward vs. when it makes a three-way merge commit, plus how to read and resolve a merge conflict.

title: Working with Remotes
summary: Sync your repo with a hosted copy: clone, add remotes, and understand the difference between fetch (download only), pull (fetch + integrate), and push (upload).

title: Meet GitHub: Repositories & Authentication
summary: Create and connect GitHub repositories, and authenticate the right way — HTTPS with a Personal Access Token or a credential manager, or SSH with a key pair (no account passwords).

title: The GitHub Flow: Branches & Pull Requests
summary: The lightweight, branch-based GitHub flow — branch, commit, push, open a pull request, review, merge — and what a pull request actually is.

title: Forking & Contributing to Open Source
summary: The fork-and-pull model: fork a repo you can't push to, add an 'upstream' remote, contribute changes via a pull request, and keep your fork in sync.

title: PR Merge Strategies: Merge, Squash & Rebase
summary: GitHub's three ways to merge a pull request — a merge commit, squash and merge, or rebase and merge — what each does to history, and when to choose which.

title: Rebasing
summary: Replay commits onto a new base for a linear history, curate history with interactive rebase (squash, reword, reorder), and respect the Golden Rule of Rebasing.

title: Resolving Conflicts in Depth
summary: Read conflicts precisely (including the ours/theirs reversal during a rebase), take a whole side with checkout --ours/--theirs, use mergetool, and let rerere replay repeated resolutions.

title: Issues, Labels, Milestones & Projects
summary: Track work on GitHub with issues, organize them with labels and milestones, plan with Projects, and auto-close issues by linking pull requests with closing keywords.

title: Tags, Releases & Semantic Versioning
summary: Mark release points with lightweight vs. annotated Git tags, publish GitHub Releases on top of them, and version software meaningfully with SemVer (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH).

title: Stash, Cherry-pick & Reflog
summary: Shelve work-in-progress with git stash, copy a single commit with git cherry-pick, and recover 'lost' commits with git reflog — Git's local safety net.

title: Rewriting History Safely
summary: Rewrite commits deliberately — amend, interactive rebase, and git filter-repo for whole-history surgery — while respecting shared history, force-pushing safely, and rotating leaked secrets.

title: Debugging History: bisect & blame
summary: Use git bisect to binary-search history for the commit that introduced a bug, git blame to see who last changed each line, and the pickaxe (log -S) to trace when code appeared.

title: Submodules & Git LFS
summary: Embed one repo inside another at a pinned commit with submodules, and keep large binaries out of history with Git LFS pointer files — plus the gotchas of each.

title: Git Internals: Objects, Refs & the DAG
summary: How Git really works: a content-addressed store of blob/tree/commit/tag objects named by hash, refs that point into them, and the commit DAG that ties it all together.

title: GitHub Actions: CI Basics
summary: GitHub's built-in CI/CD: how workflows, events, jobs, steps, runners, and actions fit together — and how to write a minimal 'test on every push' pipeline in YAML.

title: Guarding main: Branch Protection, Reviews & Hooks
summary: Protect important branches with server-side rules (required PRs, reviews, and status checks), route reviews with CODEOWNERS, and get fast local feedback from git hooks.

title: Team Workflows — Capstone
summary: Compare Git Flow, GitHub Flow, and trunk-based development, adopt a commit convention, and trace one feature end to end — tying together every lesson in the course.
